div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 808px; height: 1px; padding-top: 45px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 20px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 178px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 91px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: What status was Adam created in? Or, why was Adam created to begin with?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 135px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 93px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: In a state of original perfection and holiness, being made in the image of God

div.span: Adam was formed from the ground, made in the image and likeness of God and given the breath of life, and was placed in Eden, being tasked with its till/keep, and given the dominion over all living creatures. This is interpreted as being created in a state of original, perfect holiness and justice (elevated friendship and communion with God).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 135px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 93px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: In a state of honor and naturally inclined towards God, whose purpose is to be vicegerents on Earth

div.font: Adam was formed from the Earth and God's spirit in an honored state, being instilled with the fitrah (natural inclination towards God) and created for him and his progeny to be vicegerents (someone representing and exercising delegated power on behalf of a sovereign/ruler) on Earth. God initially places Adam in Eden to enjoy a time of bliss.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 177px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 93px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Perfect holiness and communion with God, made to be in Heaven

div.span: vs.

span.b: Honor and natural inclination towards God, made to be tested on Earth

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 288px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 121px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: What did God provide Adam with?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 230px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 123px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Preternatural gifts, dominion, a companion, and responsibility

div.span: Adam was given a garden with an abundance of accessible food and dominion over all living creatures, having the authority to name the animals himself. He was also given Eve as a companion, and the responsibility to till and keep the garden (a task that lacked toil and pain). This is interpreted as God giving Adam sanctifying grace (friendship with God), infused knowledge with preternatural gifts (ie. rightly ordered passions, freedom from suffering, immortality), and the inscription of the natural law (a rightly ordered conscience) on his heart.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 230px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 123px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Knowledge, elevated honor above the angels, a companion, a blissful life in Eden, and a warning them of Satan and how they can be expelled

div.font: Before placing Adam in Eden, God created Eve as a spouse, instilled the fitrah in him, and taught him the names of all things - knowledge the angels didn't have - and elevated him over them by commanding the angels to prostrate to him. Then, God places him in Eden, promising that he would experience bliss without hunger, thirst, scorching heat, or feeling naked or otherwise vulnerable - and with a clear warning about Satan's enmity and his desire to expel them from the garden.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 287px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 123px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Dominion, friendship with God, blissful responsibility, infused knowledge, immortality, and rightly ordered conscience

div.span: vs.

span.b: Bliss, elevated honor, taught knowledge of reality, and warning of Satan

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 423px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 131px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: What was Eden's purpose? Why did it come with a prohibition?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 360px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 133px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: A place of perfect communion, where the prohibition serves as a test of filial trust

div.span: Eden was a dwelling place for man to till and keep (as a priestly responsibility) that is pleasant to the sight and good for food. God's only prohibition was from them eating from the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, for doing so will cause them to die. This is interpreted as Eden being a holy place of perfect communion with God, where Adam is given free will and a moral test of filial trust (ie. assurance in God's love) and obedience. The choice to autonomously disobey God would then result in the loss of that sanctifying grace.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 360px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 133px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: A blissful dwelling place, where the prohibition serves as a study guide for their purpose on Earth

div.span: Eden was a dwelling place for Adam and Eve to experience bliss, ease, and to eat from whatever they wished - neither experiencing hunger, thirst, scorching heat, nor feeling naked or otherwise vulnerable. They were only prohibited from eating from a certain tree (its textual significance only in God's selection of it, in which Satan deceives them into thinking that it grants immortality and an everlasting kingdom), as well as being warned of Satan's enmity. This is interpreted as a training ground for Adam to learn what his relationship with God is, what his purpose in life is, and who his enemy is.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 422px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 133px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Permanent home of perfected communion, with the prohibition as a test/indicator of trust

div.span: vs.

span.b: Temporary home as a study guide for the Earthly test, with the prohibition as a lesson

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 543px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 101px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: What changed about Adam's state when he sinned?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 495px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 103px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Loss of innocence, sanctifying grace, and preternatural gifts

div.span: Adam's eyes were opened to his nakedness, and he covered himself out of shame. His sin resulted in his expulsion from Eden, which is interpreted as a rupture of communion: Adam effectively loses sanctifying grace, original justice/holiness, and the preternatural gifts. Human nature also becomes wounded as Adam's sin affects his progeny, where there is now a liability to suffering and death beyond Eden.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 495px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 103px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Loss of ignorance, and gaining of knowledge of his need for God's mercy

div.span: Adam's nakedness became apparent, and he covered himself out of shame. His sin (a slip within the greater context of persistent obedience) brought him out of his blissfully ignorant state - now fully understanding the consequences of his sins and his need for God's mercy, forgiveness, and grace.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 542px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 103px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Loss of innocence and sanctifying grace; ontological wounding of human nature

div.span: vs.

span.b: Loss of innocence and blissful ignorance; epistemological discovery of sin's consequences and need for God's mercy

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 658px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 111px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: What was God's immediate response to Adam's sin?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 605px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 113px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: God gives him fair, judicial curses, clothes him out of his mercy, and expels him from Eden

div.span: God questions Adam - causing his confession. Then, He pronounces judicial curses upon Adam, Eve, and the serpent that deceived them, covers them in proper clothing, and promptly expels them from Eden - barring it with a flaming sword to prevent them from returning (to return to immortality). The clothing is interpreted as a mercy within the judgement, and the judgements are interpreted to be a
fair and just response, in order to uphold the moral order by protecting humanity from perpetuating a disordered state.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 605px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 113px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: God reminds Adam of his enemy, teaches him how to repent, and accepts his repentance

div.span: God questions Adam - causing his confession. Then, God reminds Adam of Satan's enmity, tenderly teaches him how to repent for his sins, and turns towards him - accepting his repentance and forgiving him. He then informs Adam, Eve, and Satan of their temporary stay on Earth (where their livelihood was specifically prepared for them out of God's mercy) where their true test of faith will begin - with Satan as their enemy, and God as their ever-near merciful guidance, presence, and comforter.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 656px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 113px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Judicial curses, clothing out of mercy, and expulsion from Eden

div.span: vs.

span.b: Reminder of Satan's enmity, teaching of repentance, forgiveness out of mercy, and descent from Eden

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 768px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 101px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Why wasn't Adam placed back into Eden? Or - was Adam actually forgiven in that moment, or otherwise saved or pardoned from his sin's consequences?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 720px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 103px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: No, or not explicitly - forgiveness comes later as a result of Jesus

div.span: God's warning to Adam was that, if the tree was eaten from, then he would surely die - which is precisely the world we live in today, where the end of each person is death. This means that Adam was not forgiven, since the consequences of his sin were not removed. However, the real risk is spiritual death (in which we die without proper faith in God), but we are saved from this out of God's mercy in Jesus fulfilling that burden.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 720px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 103px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Yes - the descent was not a punishment, but the next step in God's plan

div.span: God's warned Adam that Satan would try to expel them from Eden, which did occur - but this was a part of God's plan from the beginning (once Adam was taught who his enemy was and how to repent), and the text explicitly states that Adam was forgiven immediately after repenting to God anyway. Satan was similarly banished from Eden, but God cursed him instead (as instead of repenting, he persisted in arrogance).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 766px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 103px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Adam wasn't forgiven from the temporal consequences, but saved from eternal, spiritual death (because of Jesus)

div.span: vs.

span.b: Adam was fully forgiven and was placed on Earth after learning the requisite knowledge to be successful

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 878px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 101px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: What state are Adam's descendants born into?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 830px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 103px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Same as Adam after the Fall: in a state of original/ancestral sin

div.span: Because Adam's Fall marks all humanity, we're all born in the same post-Fall condition that he was in: being placed on Earth (outside of Eden) and under the same judicial curses (mortality, cursed ground, pain and suffering, a world marked by sin and death). This is interpreted as us being born into a state of "original sin" or "ancestral sin" - inheriting the same consequences given to Adam.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 830px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 103px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

b.font: Same as Adam after the Fall: in a state of original forgiveness

div.span: We're all born in the same post-Fall condition that Adam was in: being placed on Earth (outside of Eden) and under the same test that was intended for all humanity. No soul bears the burden of another, so each person (including Adam) begins life with the fitrah - a pure, natural disposition towards God - only inheriting what was learned because of the descent (our needed relationship with God, with Satan as our enemy).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 876px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 103px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Just like Adam: inheriting original/ancestral sin

div.span: vs.

span.b: Just like Adam: born pure, innocent, and being naturally inclined towards God

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 985px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 106px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: On what basis are Adam and his descendants ultimately saved from their sins?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 935px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 108px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: God's grace through the death and resurrection of Christ - which reconciled humanity's penalty of sin and allowed our forgiveness - and our faith in that

div.span: Our forgiveness and salvation from ultimately come on the basis of God's grace through Jesus Christ, who died for our sins and defeated death (ie. the penalty of sin for humanity) through his resurrection. This act applies even to all who lived before Jesus (including Adam), and those who live after
receive that grace only through faith and the fulfilment of the sacraments.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 935px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 108px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: God's mercy through each person's faith, righteousness, and repentance

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: Our forgiveness and salvation ultimately comes on the basis of God's mercy and promise: for any one of us who repents, believes in God, and does good, God promises to forgive and pardon their bad deeds - for He is the Oft-Forgiving, Ever-Merciful. This applies to everyone who's ever lived, from Adam until now.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 984px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 108px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Belief in Christ as our Savior from our sins

div.span: vs.

span.b: Belief in God and His all-encompassing mercy

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 808px; height: 1px; padding-top: 108px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 18px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: 4. Which salvific narrative better fits reality?
